vat_reduced_rates.fact: Tanzania does NOT have reduced VAT rates of 5% or 10% for any product category (food, electricity, etc.) — there is no such thing as a category-based reduced VAT rate. The only rates are 18% standard, 0% zero-rated, and exempt (no VAT). SEPARATELY, a narrower 16% rate applies to a specific TRANSACTION TYPE, not a product category: B2C taxable supplies to a person in Mainland Tanzania who is NOT VAT-registered, paid through a bank or electronic payment system approved by the Commissioner General, effective 1 Sep 2025 (Finance Act 2025). This does not contradict 'no 5%/10% category rates' — it is a payment-channel/customer-type carve-out on top of the standard rate, not a reduced rate for a good or service category.

vat_withholding_goods.fact: VAT withholding on goods is 3% of the consideration (invoice value exclusive of VAT) — effective 1 July 2025 (Finance Act 2025, VAT Act s.5(5)). The standard 18% VAT rate is split: the withholding agent remits 3% to TRA and the supplier receives the remaining 15%.
vat_withholding_goods.verified_by: Finance Act 2025 (Act No. 11) s.124 amending VAT Act Cap.148 s.5(5); GN 352K of 30/6/2025 reg 31B — primary legislation, TRA-hosted
vat_withholding_goods.formula_note: The 3% applies to the CONSIDERATION (invoice value excl. VAT), NOT the VAT amount. Example: TZS 5M goods invoice, VAT = TZS 900,000; withholding = 3% x 5,000,000 = TZS 150,000 (= 1/6 of the VAT). Supplier receives the remaining 15% x 5,000,000 = TZS 750,000 of VAT (3% + 15% = 18%). NOT 3% x the VAT amount.

vat_withholding_services.fact: VAT withholding on services is 6% of the consideration (invoice value exclusive of VAT) — effective 1 July 2025 (Finance Act 2025, VAT Act s.5(5)). The standard 18% VAT rate is split: the withholding agent remits 6% to TRA and the supplier receives the remaining 12% (the statute states this 12% expressly).
vat_withholding_services.verified_by: Finance Act 2025 (Act No. 11) s.124 amending VAT Act Cap.148 s.5(5); GN 352K of 30/6/2025 reg 31B — primary legislation, TRA-hosted
vat_withholding_services.formula_note: The 6% applies to the CONSIDERATION (invoice value excl. VAT), NOT the VAT amount. Example: TZS 3M services invoice, VAT = TZS 540,000; withholding = 6% x 3,000,000 = TZS 180,000 (= 1/3 of the VAT). Supplier receives the remaining 12% x 3,000,000 = TZS 360,000 of VAT (6% + 12% = 18%). NOT 6% x the VAT amount.

wcf_disease_reporting_deadline.fact: Occupational disease reporting to WCF is a TWO-STAGE chain, not a flat 7-day deadline. Per the Workers Compensation Regulations, 2016 (GN 185/2016), Reg.16: the EMPLOYEE must notify the EMPLOYER within 14 working days of diagnosis (Reg.16(1)); the EMPLOYER must then notify WCF within 7 working days of RECEIVING that employee notice (Reg.16(2)) -- so the true worst-case window from diagnosis to WCF notification is up to 21 working days, NOT 7. Workplace death must be reported to WCF within 12 months (Reg.17(2)). Compensation claim must be filed within 12 months of accident or disease discovery (Reg.19(1)).

wcf_disease_reporting_deadline.correction_note: Prior fact stated a flat 7 working days from diagnosis, sourced only to the wcf.go.tz portal page (no regulation citation). Re-verified 2026-08-29 against GN 185/2016 Reg.16 directly: the 7-working-day figure is real but attaches to the EMPLOYER's leg after receiving the employee's notice, not to the diagnosis date itself -- the employee has a separate, prior 14-working-day window to notify the employer first. Root cause: the portal-sourced summary compressed a two-step regulatory chain into its second step only, understating the true diagnosis-to-WCF window by up to two-thirds (7 vs 21 working days). This is the highest-harm correction in this batch: a wrong deadline surfaces when a real claim is refused for being late, not when someone checks arithmetic.

efd_threshold_tzs_11m.fact: EFD (fiscal receipt) issuance is the DEFAULT LEGAL REQUIREMENT for every person who supplies goods or renders services, REGARDLESS OF TURNOVER (Tax Administration Act, Cap.438 R.E.2023, s.44(1) 'Issuance of Fiscal Receipt' -- renumbered from s.36 in the R.E.2019 edition by Finance Act 2023 s.54). The ONLY exemption mechanism is a Commissioner-General public notice, published in a newspaper of wide circulation or other public media, naming a specific person or class of persons excluded from the requirement (s.44(2)) -- there is NO turnover threshold written anywhere in this section, or anywhere else in the Act. A person actually excluded by such a notice issues a manual receipt instead (s.44(3)-(4)). REJECT both TZS 11,000,000 and TZS 14,000,000 as 'the EFD threshold': both figures are real, but they are the turnover BAND EDGES in the Income Tax Act's PRESUMPTIVE INCOME TAX table (First Schedule, para.2(3)) -- a different provision entirely, about tax rates for individuals who don't keep adequate records, not about EFD issuance. Practitioner guides (RSM, Habib, Auditax, VATupdate) appear to have conflated the two because both sit in the same Part of the same Act. CORRECT ANSWER to 'do I need an EFD at my turnover?': 'Ndiyo, kwa default -- isipokuwa TRA imetoa taarifa rasmi (Commissioner-General public notice) inayokuondolea wewe/kundi lako. Thibitisha na TRA kama taarifa hiyo inakuhusu.' (Yes, by default -- unless TRA has issued a public notice exempting you/your class. Confirm with TRA whether such a notice applies to you.) This is a correct, non-hedging answer, not an evasion -- turnover does not change it.
efd_threshold_tzs_11m.correct_value: EFD is required BY DEFAULT for everyone, regardless of turnover (s.44(1)). Exemption is ONLY by CG public notice naming a class (s.44(2)), never by a turnover figure. TZS 11M and TZS 14M are NOT EFD thresholds -- both are presumptive-income-tax band edges (Income Tax Act First Schedule para.2(3)), a different provision.

vat_withholding_formula_correct.fact: VAT withholding rate applies to the CONSIDERATION (invoice value exclusive of VAT), NOT the VAT amount. The standard 18% VAT is split between TRA and the supplier. Goods: 3% x consideration withheld, supplier receives 15% x consideration (3 + 15 = 18). Services: 6% x consideration withheld, supplier receives 12% x consideration (6 + 12 = 18). Example goods: TZS 5M invoice, VAT = TZS 900,000; withholding = 3% x 5,000,000 = TZS 150,000; supplier receives TZS 750,000 of the VAT. Example services: TZS 3M invoice, VAT = TZS 540,000; withholding = 6% x 3,000,000 = TZS 180,000; supplier receives TZS 360,000 of the VAT.
vat_withholding_formula_correct.correct_value: 3% of consideration for goods (supplier 15%); 6% of consideration for services (supplier 12%)

osha_vs_wcf_roles.fact: OSHA and WCF are two separate institutions with different roles. OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Authority) registers workplaces (s.16, OSH Act No.5 of 2003, before commencing operations), inspects, and issues the annual Compliance Licence; OSHA does NOT pay injury compensation. Compensation for occupational injuries and diseases is paid by the WCF (Workers Compensation Fund) under the Workers Compensation Act, Cap 263, funded by the employer's 0.5% monthly wage contribution. OSHA registration and WCF registration are separate obligations and both apply. WCF applies from the first employee — there is NO 2-employee or other minimum-count threshold for WCF.

brela_business_structures.fact: BRELA registers businesses in THREE main legal forms: (1) sole proprietorship / individual — registered as a business name under the Business Names (Registration) Act Cap.213; (2) partnership (firm) — also registered as a business name under Cap.213 (a firm is two or more persons in partnership); (3) limited liability company — incorporated under the Companies Act Cap.212. The choice between a business name and a company depends on the desired legal structure and liability, NOT on the number of employees or the amount of capital — there is no employee-count or capital threshold that forces incorporation. BRELA separately administers trademarks, patents and industrial designs (intellectual property); these are NOT business structures.

gn487a_mgeni_cap357_definition.fact: GN487A defines 'non-citizen' by reference to the Tanzania Citizenship Act Cap.357 R.E.2023. Cap.357 recognises three citizen categories: citizen by birth, citizen by descent, and citizen by naturalisation. A person holding Tanzanian citizenship under any of these three categories is NOT a non-citizen for GN487A purposes. Whether dual nationals holding a Tanzanian passport qualify as citizens depends on Cap.357 — this is a legal interpretation that must be verified with an immigration lawyer.

council_service_levy_is_a_cap_not_a_rate.fact: Ushuru wa huduma wa halmashauri (service levy): sheria inaweka KIKOMO cha asilimia 0.3 ya mauzo (bila VAT na ushuru wa bidhaa) — si kiwango kimoja cha kitaifa. Kila halmashauri hupanga chake kwa sheria ndogo, na nyingi hutoza chini ya kikomo hicho. Uliza ofisi ya mapato ya halmashauri yako kwa kiwango halisi.
council_service_levy_is_a_cap_not_a_rate.correct_value: a CEILING of 0.3% of turnover net of VAT and excise — not a rate

council_service_levy_non_corporate_confl.fact: Je mfanyabiashara mmoja mmoja hulipa ushuru wa huduma? Sheria yenyewe inagongana. Kifungu 7(1)(u) cha Cap 290 kinasema hulipwa na "corporate entities au mtu yeyote anayefanya biashara akiwa na leseni", lakini Jedwali la sheria hiyo hiyo linakataza halmashauri kutoza wasio-corporate. Duka la mtu mmoja ni non-corporate. Uliza halmashauri yako na omba maelezo kwa maandishi.
council_service_levy_non_corporate_confl.correct_value: the operative section and the Schedule disagree — do not state a single answer
council_service_levy_non_corporate_confl.source_note: Cap 290 s.7(1)(u) versus the Schedule made under s.16(1), whose "shall not impose" column lists non-corporate entities. A sole-proprietor duka is non-corporate. No phrasing on our side resolves a conflict inside the statute.

market_dues_no_national_amount.fact: Ushuru wa soko au genge ni kiasi gani? Hakuna kiwango kimoja cha kitaifa. Kiasi hupangwa chini ya Sheria ya Masoko (Cap 106) na sheria ndogo za kila halmashauri — zaidi ya halmashauri 180, kila moja na yake, na hubadilika mara kwa mara. Uliza meneja wa soko au ofisi ya mapato ya halmashauri yako.

business_licence_fee_national_schedule_l.fact: Leseni ya biashara inagharimu kiasi gani? Ada imepangwa KITAIFA chini ya Sheria ya Leseni za Biashara, lakini leseni hutolewa na kukusanywa na halmashauri, na halmashauri hairuhusiwi kutoza zaidi ya ada iliyopangwa. Ada hutegemea aina ya biashara na eneo — jiji/manispaa, wilaya/mji, au kijiji — na kama ni leseni kuu au ya tawi. Uliza halmashauri yako kwa ada ya aina yako.
business_licence_fee_national_schedule_l.correct_value: fee set nationally, licence issued and collected locally; council may not exceed the prescribed fee
business_licence_fee_national_schedule_l.source_note: Cap 290 Schedule: a council MAY charge the "Business Licence fee for general merchandising as prescribed under the Business Licensing Act", and "Fees exceeding the prescribed fee" sits in the SHALL-NOT-IMPOSE column. Schedule structure (2014 text): ~31 categories, priced by geography tier and principal-vs-subsidiary, local and foreign columns. A duka sits in category 29, General Trading.
